title: Grateful Dead Live at Milwaukee Performing Arts Center on 1972-10-24
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD

ai_review.summary: Excellent Miller‑mastered soundboard capture of a fire‑filled 1972 show highlighted by a monster The Other One and a soaring Phil “stomp”.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised across the board for its superb, near‑perfect mix – long uninterrupted jams, barely‑noticeable patches and crystal‑clear balance of Jerry, Bob, Phil and Bill. Musically the performance shines with an epic The Other One, a jam‑heavy He's Gone and what reviewers call one of the best “Philo stomps” of the fall‑’72 era, delivering high energy from start to finish.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviews are 4–5 stars and unanimously praise both the musical performance (standout jams, The Other One) and the recording quality (superb Miller mix).

recording_quality.technical_notes: Miller’s masterful soundboard mix is described as crisp, superb and nearly perfect; patches are seamless and the longer tracks preserve uninterrupted jams.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A flowing, expansive set with extended improvisations; the Phil‑centric jam (the “Philo stomp”) and the climactic end of He's Gone drive the momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mentioned positively as part of the flawless mix – guitar tone praised implicitly.
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly highlighted for gorgeous bass themes and a standout “Philo stomp” that defines this show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Included in the praise for the overall balanced mix; no specific performance comment.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming noted as part of the superb mix, though without detailed remarks.
